subject: Anchored rate bands & surge smoothing approach for MEDSYS RFP — pricing deliverable

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Anchored rate bands & surge smoothing approach for MEDSYS RFP — pricing deliverable

Hi Elena — attaching the pricing deliverable we discussed this morning. High-level summary below; full math and worked examples are in the attachment (Redwood_Anchored-Ratebands_and_Surge-Smoothing_v1.pdf) and the usage scenarios workbook.

Quick summary (commercial highlights):
- Anchored rate bands: a baseline monthly commit (M tokens) is used to anchor the monthly unit price; bands allow +/- 20% natural variance without stepping to a higher price band.
- Base token price (anchor): $0.00060 per token for the baseline model (LlamaX-8B-quant).
- Tiered commit discounts: incremental volume discounts at 1.5x, 3x, and 6x baseline with step-downs to $0.00048, $0.00042, and $0.00036 respectively.
- Burst credit bucket: 30% of committed monthly tokens available for short-term bursts at the anchor price (consumed first before overage charging).
- Smoothing window: 3-month delta smoothing — monthly overshoots/undershoots are averaged across a rolling 3-month window to determine any true-up.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up (following the smoothing window). Credits carry forward for 12 months if unused.
- Overage policy: sustained growth above smoothed commit triggers overage pricing at anchored bands unless customer elects to convert to a higher commit tier. Overages above burst bucket charged at 1.25x anchor price for the month, with mitigation credits for spikes caused by operational testing.

Why this structure: it protects MEDSYS from abrupt rate jumps during normal seasonality while allowing predictable economics for Redwood. The attached file has two example months and a 6-month projection under your sample traffic from the workbook.

Next steps: if this aligns, Marissa will prepare a term sheet and a DocuSign-ready PO/draft contract. If you have specific thresholds you'd like to widen/narrow (e.g., +/-15% rather than 20%), we can tune the band and show impact on unit economics.

Attachments: Redwood_Anchored-Ratebands_and_Surge-Smoothing_v1.pdf, MEDSYS_usage-scenarios_v2.xlsx

Thanks — I’m available for a short walkthrough early next week.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
https://www.redwood.ai

Dylan — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions before we take this to procurement: 

1) On the burst credit bucket: does the 30% allocation renew monthly or is it a rolling pool tied to the 3-month smoothing window? If we have a one-off spike in month 2 of a quarter, how is that consumed versus month 1 credits?
2) For the 3-month smoothing window and quarterly true-up: can you show an example where month pattern = [100%, 140%, 80%] of baseline? How does the overage compute and are there any credits applied?
3) Are the anchored band thresholds (the +/- 20%) tunable by contract and do they affect the discount breakpoints?

Also — we have an internal compliance requirement: any capped overage mechanism needs an audit trail per invoice (i.e., token-level sampling and explanation for the month). Can you confirm Redwood can produce that export for our finance/audit team?

If you could respond with short answers and updated example sheet, we’ll schedule a procurement review for Thursday 19th.

Best,

Subject: Re: Anchored rate bands & surge smoothing approach for MEDSYS RFP — pricing deliverable

Elena — great questions, answered inline below. I’ve also attached a quick 3-line worked example in the workbook and updated the PDF to fully call out audit exports.

1) Burst credit bucket lifecycle:
- The 30% allocation is applied per calendar month and renews monthly. It is consumed first for any spikes within that month. Unused burst credits do NOT roll forward as burst, however they factor into the 3-month smoothing calculation as "consumed vs committed" for credit/true-up math.
- Example: Month 1 uses 20% of burst, Month 2 uses 40% (i.e., consumes 10% from above the 30% bucket and triggers overage for that portion). The workbook shows token flow in columns E-G.

2) 3-month smoothing worked example ([100%, 140%, 80%] of baseline):
- Baseline = 1,000,000 tokens/mo (for example).
- Month volumes = [1,000,000; 1,400,000; 800,000] -> rolling 3-month average = (1,000,000 + 1,400,000 + 800,000) / 3 = 1,066,667 tokens/month.
- Quarterly true-up compares smoothed average vs committed baseline (1,066,667 vs 1,000,000) -> net delta = +66,667 tokens for quarter -> true-up charge applies on that delta.
- Burst bucket consumed first: the 30% monthly buckets (300k tokens/month) are consumed in months 1-3 per the rules. Month 2’s 400k over baseline consumes 300k burst + 100k overage. The smoothing math credits Month 3’s lower consumption partly against that overage during the quarterly true-up.
- Net effect: overage billed at anchored band price for the net delta after smoothing, with any burst-eligible portion billed at anchor price and non-burst overage at 1.25x anchor price (per proposal). See workbook sheet 'WorkedExamples'.

3) Tunability of anchored bands:
- Yes — the +/- 20% band is a contract parameter. Narrowing to +/- 15% reduces the supplier revenue risk and would increase the anchor price roughly ~3–6% depending on your baseline volatility. We included an "impact matrix" in the workbook that shows the anchor price adjustment for +/- 10/15/20/25% bands across 3 volatility profiles.

4) Audit/export capability (compliance):
- Redwood can deliver an invoice-attached CSV export showing sampled token-level counts, model variant used, route (hosted/dedicated), and the policy tag (burst vs committed vs overage). We provide a daily rollup and can provide a 1% random token sample payload log under an NDA if required. The updated PDF calls out the export format and fields.

Next steps: 
- I’ve updated the workbook per your sample pattern and the PDF to include the audit export spec. Marissa will prepare a concise term-sheet and a DocuSign package once you confirm the band parameter and whether the 30% burst is acceptable as a monthly renew.

Link to updated workbook + examples: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-9876543 (attachments section)

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
